name: Server-side request forgery
mental_model: Untrusted input influences where a server-side fetcher connects, allowing the server's network position to cross a destination boundary.
security_property: Server-side requests must be restricted to canonical, revalidated destinations allowed for the exact feature and action.
root_causes: User-controlled destination without a strict allowlist
Validation before redirects or resolution changes
Access to internal or metadata address classes
signals: A server fetches a user-supplied destination
Destination checks differ before and after canonicalization
Internal-only response characteristics appear in a controlled simulation

hypothesis_templates.statement: When {actor} supplies {destination} to {fetch_feature}, the server may reach {controlled_resource} outside the permitted destination class.
preconditions: Only a dictionary-backed local fetcher is used
No DNS, socket, redirect, or real destination is contacted
hypothesis_templates.expected_safe_behaviour: Canonical destination policy rejects the controlled internal-only resource.
hypothesis_templates.expected_vulnerable_behaviour: The synthetic server retrieves the controlled internal-only resource.
hypothesis_templates.falsifier: Every canonicalization, redirect, and resolution state remains within the declared destination policy.
stop_conditions: Credentials or metadata would be involved

safe_test_pattern: Exercise only a dictionary-backed local fetcher with named public and internal resource classes; no URL is resolved and no socket is opened.
positive_controls: An allowlisted synthetic public resource is retrieved
negative_controls: The controlled internal-only resource is denied by destination policy
falsifiers: The feature never performs server-side retrieval
Canonical destination policy denies every controlled internal class

minimum_evidence.description: Synthetic requested destination and exact dictionary-backed retrieval result.
Declared public and internal-only destination classes for the fixture.
Allowlisted-resource positive control and internal-resource denial control.
Deterministic repeat with the same local resource map.
Human statement limited to the controlled destination-class violation.

common_false_positives: A reflected URL with no server fetch
A response generated locally without crossing a destination policy
impact_boundaries: A fetch signal does not prove access to cloud metadata or internal services
Destination control does not prove credential exposure
minimum_impact_rules: No network, DNS, redirects, or real URLs in the fixture
Never request metadata, credentials, or third-party systems
remediation: Canonicalize and revalidate every redirect and resolution
Deny private, loopback, link-local, and metadata classes at the broker
programme_policy_considerations: Treat live SSRF testing as a separate posture decision
Do not use collaboration or third-party interaction services by default

revisions.summary: Initial destination-policy card and socket-free synthetic fetch fixture.
